extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing clinical case reports; journal editors and peer reviewers of case reports; clinicians who write case reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and reporting clinical case reports for publication, specifying the items authors should include to ensure completeness and transparency. Intended to standardize narrative, clinical, diagnostic, therapeutic, outcome, and ethical elements of a published case report.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: A case report tells a story in a narrative format that includes the presenting concerns, clinical findings, diagnoses, interventions, outcomes (including adverse events), and follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrative should include a discussion of the rationale for any conclusions and any takeaway messages; use prose with a consistent style across all sections. Strike a balance between adequate detail and concise writing. The checklist is structured to capture useful clinical information (including “meaningful use” information mandated by some insurance plans).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: The words 'case report' (or 'case study') should appear in the title along with phenomenon of greatest interest (eg, symptom, diagnosis, test, intervention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the phenomenon of greatest interest explicit in the title so readers and indexers can identify the focus quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: The key elements of this case in 2 to 5 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose 2–5 succinct keywords that capture the main clinical elements to improve discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract—Introduction—What does this case add? Case Presentation: Main symptoms of the patient; Main clinical findings; Main diagnoses and interventions; Main outcomes. Conclusion—What were the main takeaway lessons from this case?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the abstract to state what the case adds, summarize the case presentation (symptoms, findings, diagnoses, interventions, outcomes) and end with clear takeaway lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief background summary of this case referencing the relevant medical literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the case is noteworthy and situate it in the context of existing literature; cite relevant sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Demographic information (eg, age, gender, ethnicity, occupation); Main symptoms of the patient (his or her chief complaints); Medical, family, and psychosocial history—including diet, lifestyle, and genetic information whenever possible and details about relevant comorbidities including past interventions and their outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient demographic and history details to understand the patient context while de-identifying as required by journal/patient privacy standards. Include relevant comorbidities and prior treatments with outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the relevant physical examination (PE) findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report key examination findings that support diagnoses and management decisions; focus on findings pertinent to the case narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Depict important dates and times in this case (table or figure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a timeline (item 7) in the form of a table or figure giving specific dates/times of key events (eg, family and past medical history entries, genetic info, symptoms onset, diagnostic test dates/results, interventions, events during follow-up). The timeline should show how the key events of the case unfolded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic methods (eg, PE, laboratory testing, imaging, questionnaires); Diagnostic challenges (eg, financial, language/cultural); Diagnostic reasoning including other diagnoses considered; Prognostic characteristics (eg, staging) where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the methods used for diagnosis, any barriers or challenges, the reasoning process (differential diagnoses considered), and prognostic information when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Therapeutic Intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of intervention (eg, pharmacologic, surgical, preventive, self-care); Administration of intervention (eg, dosage, strength, duration); Changes in intervention (with rationale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail the intervention(s) thoroughly (what, how, dose/strength/duration), and document any changes over time along with the reasons for changes to allow replication or comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up and Outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize the clinical course of all follow-up visits, including clinician- and patient-assessed outcomes; Important follow-up test results (positive or negative); Intervention adherence and tolerability (and how this was assessed); Adverse and unanticipated events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the complete follow-up course, objective and subjective outcome measures, adherence/tolerability data and method of assessment, and any adverse or unexpected events to provide transparency on outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengths and limitations of the management of this case; Relevant medical literature; Rationale for conclusions (including assessments of cause and effect); Main takeaway lessons of this case report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically appraise the case management, relate findings to the literature, justify conclusions (noting limits of causal inference for single cases), and state clear lessons or implications for practice or research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient Perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: The patient should share his or her perspective or experience whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include patient-reported outcomes or experiences when feasible; developers advocated for patient-reported outcomes and experiences whenever possible and discussed need for guidance on patient-reported outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed Consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the patient give informed consent? Please provide if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors have an ethical duty to obtain informed consent to publish patient information. Consent becomes informed when the patient or a relative reads the case report and approves its contents. If the patient cannot give consent and proxy consent attempts have failed, seek permission to publish from an institutional committee. There may be circumstances where ethics committee or IRB approval is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other common journal requirements (not part of CARE checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical journals often require authors to address potential competing interests; de-identification of patient-related data; and ethics committee or IRB approval if obtained or necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not included in the CARE checklist, authors should declare competing interests, ensure patient data are de-identified per journal/policy requirements, and report any ethics or IRB approvals or statement if required.
